lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A cross between a bear and an owl that hugs like a bear and attacks with its beak; Baldur's Gate 3 lists owlbears among its Forgotten Realms monsters.

from.quote: An owlbear is depicted as a cross between a bear and an owl, which "hugs" like a bear and attacks with its beak.
The game features monsters from the Forgotten Realms, including owlbears, gnolls, and mind flayers.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: The tabletop books describe owlbears as carnivorous and famed for aggression and ferocity. They live in mated pairs in caves and hunt any creature bigger than a mouse.

from.quote: owlbears are carnivorous creatures, famed for their aggression and ferocity; they live in mated pairs in caves and hunt any creature bigger than a mouse.

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A drow paladin who leads a band of goblins and other creatures for the game's antagonist in the first act and clashes with the Emerald Grove refugee settlement.

from.quote: Race || Drow
Class || Paladin
she leads a band of goblins and other creatures in service of the game's antagonist
This brings her into conflict with a refugee settlement called the Emerald Grove

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Your choices are to help her raid the grove, to oppose and kill her and her goblins, or to avoid the raid and keep her alive by knocking her out with non-lethal damage while killing her commanders, or by ignoring her.

from.quote: the player may either help her raid it or oppose and kill her and her goblins
the player may avoid the raid entirely and keep her alive by either knocking her out with non-lethal damage while killing her commanders or ignoring her entirely

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Avoiding the raid means the grove is slaughtered off-screen; siding with her or keeping her alive lets her reach act two, where she can be rescued and become a full companion.

from.quote: though this option will cause the grove to be slaughtered off-screen

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A common, fairly weak race of evil humanoid monsters in the tabletop game; in the first act a goblin horde that worships a cult of the Absolute faces the druids and tiefling refugees of the Emerald Grove.

from.quote: goblins are a common and fairly weak race of evil humanoid monsters
local druids and tiefling refugees face off against the goblin horde that worships a cult of the "Absolute"

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: The first-edition tabletop monster book describes goblins as a tribal society in dismal surroundings, and low-level characters often face them. The first act's locations include a goblin camp, and Minthara leads a band of goblins in that act.

from.quote: The goblin appears in the first edition Monster Manual (1977), where it is described as having a tribal society and dwelling in dismal surroundings.

lines.text: Drinkable items, including health potions and one that lets you talk to animals.

as if they are a health potion

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: Drinking a potion consumes a bonus action; attacking with a sword or casting a spell consumes an action.

from.quote: Major instructions to a character, like attacking with a sword or casting a spell, consume an action. Smaller commands, like jumping or drinking a potion, consume a bonus action.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Actions, bonus actions and movement are separate turn resources, so a potion does not cost you your attack or spell.

from.quote: The primary resources are actions, bonus actions, and movement.
